Nine open-loop sensor replays of three physically valid witness trajectories expose an observability gap during the turn. Two settings of fixed command smoothing produced 24/24 full random stress episodes without a stop, hardware violation or contract problem in v4. body.text: The PPO baseline is r0057, paired with iteration r0056 and package SHA a44fa6a0118e…. Both official failure montages, 1367139607 and 1506359875, show the palm drifting away from the grounded plug by 2.50 s. Fingers change posture in free space and no enclosure develops throughout the clips. All 64 trials ran without hardware violations or stops, 22 pass the final hand-rest check, and sandbox act p99 is 0.529 ms. I delivered it as the first incumbent at 07:28:06 UTC to obtain early target evidence. The six-minute checkpoint also has no lift and loses the rest check on all 64 fixed starts. The first three full-witness command projections give one lift under the pilot envelope and three under the wider position/finger envelope, with no turn in either, which motivates measuring command authority after the target replay.

The continuous-impedance simulator preview passes all published station thresholds. Its blocked finger retains 0.346 rad of command error and full effort without a violation, and the published drift warning reports 0.076 rad over two seconds. Applying three old exact full plans gives three lifts and no turns. New batched physics proposals with the continuous arm produce exact qualifying turns for grip scales 0.34, 0.62 and 0.90. Further exact replays carry each upright into the goal with zero unsupported contact gaps. This preview is separate from the delivered v4 baseline. In the tested v4 baseline, removing previous-target smoothing gives six hardware violations on 16 paired local starts versus zero with smoothing, so the next envelope should retain causal rate bounds while allowing stronger sustained squeeze.

The first PPO branch met its predeclared stop condition at 15 minutes. Zero qualifying lifts appeared across the fixed 64-start evaluations at two, six and twelve minutes, and no full-start lift appeared in the training funnel through 936,960 steps. The mean enclosure reward and lift progress stayed within a few ten-thousandths per step while KL stayed around 0.03. More time on this branch would mostly repeat failures. The early deliverable remains r0057, and its first target round is pending. The next training experiment will be determined after the full target judgment and replay, with separate attention to consequential approach potential, physical model contact safety, and finger command authority.

body.observation_mismatch: All 4,800 target pose samples are valid. All eight v4 replays start at the exact t=0 estimated position and orientation from the station log, with no occlusion. Target-to-true simulated object center RMSE is 0.933 to 1.409 mm by trial, while independent replay sensor estimates differ by 1.148 to 1.568 mm RMSE. Median across trials of the median and 95th percentile pose age is 43.3/53.3 ms in the target and 56.9/62.2 ms in replay. No trial crosses 20 mm object-center difference. Tilt comparison is also reported along the blade axis to respect the estimator's 180° flip symmetry.
body.dynamics_mismatch: The v4 open-loop replays use all 600 sent commands and the original package ramp. Wrist position RMSE is 0.629 to 0.654 mm and finger encoder RMSE is 0.067 to 0.074 rad. All eight target trials and all eight replays show a grounded plug and no torque spike or stop. The selected start is nominal for unknown contact properties. This round provides no grasp or contact dynamics evidence.
body.changes: Record the baseline motion retreat as a learned approach failure. Split the ramp deadband from a signed loss that penalizes withdrawal beyond it, give one-time credit for physical opposed enclosure, and test a closer pregrasp pose with full task-start support. Benchmark the continuous-impedance dynamics against this replay and the published blocked-finger test before adopting them. Keep both v3 contract rate limits and closed-loop safety checks.

body.text: After r0063 and r0064, I compared the full eight target command streams under both arm models and under shorter hand delay and lower grip. Median wrist error is 0.637 mm in v4 and 0.655 mm in the continuous model. Median finger encoder error is 0.071 and 0.072 rad, respectively. Neither the tested shorter delay nor lower grip improves encoder fit, and no trial contains hand–plug contact to identify the contact parameters. The approach retreat reproduces under each model. I am adopting continuous impedance for its independent station calibration and verified in-hand physics, with prior grip and delay ranges and the standard sensor retained for the next training experiment. Local continuous-model feasibility is 24/32 on a second, entirely fresh set, with zero violations and stops.

The gate renderer failed after the reproducible evaluation because its World constructor rejected the preloaded model. I recreated all four selected review rollouts under the exact physical evaluator. Both failures hold the start fallback after the search finds no complete safe sequence. Both successes grasp near 2.38 s, hold the plug in the air by 4.98 s, and leave it upright by 10.18 s. reward_terms.name: reference_fingers

reward_terms.name: slip

reward_terms.name: action_rate

reward_terms.name: push

reward_terms.name: safety
reward_terms.formula: Squared normalized torque margin beyond 12 N·m and near-limit finger margin. Only penalties from physical state.

body.text: Task baseline r0074 repeats one qualifying lift on 64 fresh starts, with zero stops and hardware violations, 40 final hand-rest passes, and a 0.287 ms sandbox p99. It was delivered as s02. I viewed both gate-selected failed starts using a local rerender with independent standard sensor draws because the frozen gate renderer still fails. In 1475831798 and 471888336 the fingers make contact at about 0.30 and 0.27 s, the plug shifts 41 and 44 mm along the table, and clearance stays below 0.2 mm before the palm retreats. Removing the encoder-target residual features at the same weights raises local lifts from one to two of 64, with no stops or violations in either group. This small unpaired stage-count difference does not establish a feature advantage. The training funnel has several stochastic lifts and partial reward improvement, so the scheduled PPO run continues while the target round measures whether the sliding and contact repeat.

Correction to r0075. The encoder-target residual ablation is paired on the same 64 starts and sensor draws. The ablation lifts on seeds 353604967 and 1249815122, while the original lifts on seed 335814359. Two gains and one loss leave the direction unresolved.

body.text: Checkpoint 0351 improved fixed-start lift to 16/64 with unchanged training. Its first clearance-and-rise interval starts near 1.27 s on the 16 lift cases and stays continuously opposed for a median 0.28 s after that row. The thumb is the first or tied lost contact in 12 of 16. Seven losses occur while the plug was visible throughout the interval. The selected local non-lift and lift replays let the existing reward pay +0.699 and +0.126 for grounded pushes, +7.349 for a lift followed by loss, and +50.705 for the complete witness. In 31071524 the fingertips engage by 0.09 s and drive the plug about 56 mm across the support, with under 0.05 mm clearance. In 289604245 the thumb opposes the other digits by 0.74 s and briefly moves the plug above 10 mm at 1.36–1.42 s before losing it. The actor is already commanding up, so clipping its lower finger target cannot explain the fault. Test higher contract start poses by 6, 10 and 14 mm with the same actor and nominal action bounds. Predict a zero-violation lift gain over the incumbent if the smallest safe change retains the early approach. Keep the ongoing PPO run unchanged. A separately preflighted reward for retained opposition and rest is planned after the allocated branch.

Keep the frozen task suite and physical adjacent fingers. Resting earns no positive return. All three complete witnesses still receive each ordered bonus.

body.text: Predeclare a 100-minute signed-retention PPO continuation from a single actor whose lineage began at random weights, with checkpoint 1089 and package C as the default parent if no later safe checkpoint improves the stage funnel. Keep the exact observation history, action transform and full deployment plus five physical reset probabilities of the selected parent. Configure the critic and optimizer afresh for the changed objective. Signed opposed clearance and unqualified turn potentials reverse on loss. A grounded sliding penalty removes the measured shortcut, while untouched upright support and measured rest give the late reset phases a learnable effect. Expect a lifted hold longer than the 0.28 s median seen in r0077 and at least one qualifying turn in a deployment rollout. At the 20-minute checkpoint stop only if fixed evaluation has no qualifying lift, no gain in opposed-hold duration and no subsequent stage on the paired reset probes. At 40 minutes stop only if turn remains absent in both full and assisted episodes and opposed duration has flattened. Otherwise continue to budget or a verified stopping condition. Every kept package still uses the official frozen numerical evaluator and a fresh gate.

reward_terms.name: touchdown

reward_terms.name: release

reward_terms.name: placed
reward_terms.formula: Terminal bonus for the continuous ordered skill, throughout the last half second inside the exact stability and rest bounds.

reward_terms.name: reference_object

reward_terms.name: reference_wrist

reward_terms.name: failure

body.text: Reviewed the r0113 near-turn image on seed 1941669301. The thumb and middle oppose at 2.76 s with 132.9 degrees opposition, 98.2 mm bottom clearance and 29.38 degrees blade tilt. Neither is touching by 2.80 s. The plug returns to the table by 3.0 s. This is the same failure mode as the early retention actor with a larger controlled angular excursion. A second exact full-start training-only turn appears at update 661. It runs all 600 calls without a safety or contract event and loses grip before carry. The deterministic evaluations still show zero turns and zero placements.

Independent whole-episode preflight of the fixed middle MCP2 bound at −0.05 rad reaches 107/128 opposed lifts and 128/128 terminal hand rests. No finger turn, carry, placement, stop, hardware or contract event occurs. curriculum.description: Settled randomized positions and velocities only. Reward phase is allowed to skip earlier conditions in intermediate reset episodes. Deployment resets use the full 1.5 s ramp, full task criteria and 20 s horizon.

live_pickup.description: A prior PPO checkpoint runs a short monitored deployment prefix. Training begins in the resulting opposed grasp with its live actuator, sensor and causal actor history. The prefix supplies environment context. Its actions never enter PPO batches. Other reset modes retain their original fractions.

reference.startup: Per-trial adaptation from true fixed task start and goal (0.425, −0.068, −0.2935) m.
reference.shaping: State-driven phase reference tracking with symmetric object keypoints, reachable wrist and tolerated finger posture. Phase changes on simulated physical criteria.

checks.station_model: Simulation v5 has zero failures in the published station scenarios. The blocked index retains sustained torque and reports a residual drift warning.
checks.hardware_response: Contract monitor enforces each 100 Hz state and policy row. Stop, hardware, contract or nonfinite state ends the training episode. Fallen-below-table objects also terminate the training episode.
checks.reward_tolerances: 40 mm keypoints, 100 mm and 45° on palm pose, 0.44 rad median posture. The retargeted palm cue lies near 90 mm above actual contacts on this embodiment.

body.text: The capture-aligned feature implementation adds 36 causal palm-relative components to the 608-input PPO actor. The original feature prefix is bit-identical on two complete rollouts. With new input columns initialized to zero, the largest action change across 1,200 contract observations is 2.0e−8. A three-update diagnostic build validates v3 at p99 0.984 ms with no time input. It is not being judged for task success. The paired context branches and the pending target package remain unchanged.
